description: Implement a real 3-state (closed/open/half-open) circuit breaker in place of a stub that always calls through
prompts: breaker.js's CircuitBreaker.call(fn, now) always just calls fn() - there is no breaking logic at all. Implement the real 3-state machine: the constructor takes (failureThreshold, resetTimeout). Starts CLOSED. In CLOSED, call(fn, now) invokes fn(); if it throws, count consecutive failures, and once `failureThreshold` CONSECUTIVE failures have happened, trip to OPEN (recording when it opened) and re-throw. While OPEN, call(fn, now) must NOT invoke fn() at all and must instead throw a CircuitOpenError - UNLESS at least `resetTimeout` seconds have passed since it opened, in which case it moves to HALF_OPEN and allows exactly ONE trial call: if that call succeeds, go back to CLOSED (reset the failure count); if it throws, go back to OPEN and RESET the open-time to `now` (so the next trial is only allowed after another full resetTimeout, not immediately). Export CircuitOpenError alongside CircuitBreaker.
name: add_js_circuit_breaker_state_machine
